title: Stumptown Hair Bender review: an espresso blend that can also serve drip
description: A research-led US Hair Bender review covering its changing blend, roaster flavor notes, espresso and drip use, freshness, 12 oz and 5 lb value, and tradeoffs.
imageAlt: Official Stumptown Hair Bender coffee bag
imageCredit: Official Stumptown product photograph for identification; Coffeedant has not photographed or tasted this bag.
verdict: Hair Bender is a useful first bag for a household that makes espresso and drip with one coffee. Stumptown designs it as its café espresso blend yet explicitly recommends pour-over, drip and French press. Its citrus, dark chocolate and raisin words are the roaster's brief, not a Coffeedant tasting result; choose it if that mix sounds better than a strictly low-acid, roast-forward shot.
bestFor: One whole-bean coffee for portafilter espresso and filter brewing
A chocolate-led blend that still has a citrus direction
Buyers who will compare 12 oz freshness before committing to 5 lb
skipIf: You want a fixed farm, variety and process on every shipment
Citrus in espresso is something you dislike even after dialing in
You need a ready-ground espresso option from this direct listing
authorNote: I compared Stumptown's current product and blend records with its brew and storage advice, then read attributable owner disagreement. The recommendation is about purchase fit, not my own tasting.

sections.title: An espresso recipe, not a fixed lot
paragraphs: Stumptown calls Hair Bender its signature espresso blend and says it is used in its cafés. The identity is a continuing recipe, not a promise that every component farm remains the same. Its current product page names Latin America, East Africa and Indonesia, while the roaster's blend account explains how washed American coffees provide a sweet base, East African coffees bring floral complexity and semi-washed Indonesian coffees add body. These are sourcing and formulation statements from Stumptown. They do not establish the exact farm or variety in the bag you receive. [1] [2]

The signature-blend collection calls Hair Bender medium/dark, while the product listing emphasizes its flavor direction rather than a numerical roast measurement. Use that classification to compare shelves, but read the roast date on the actual bag. A changing blend can aim for a steady cup while its components move with harvests. If lot-level traceability is the main reason you buy coffee, a current single-origin listing is a better starting point. [3]

sections.title: Chocolate is the anchor; citrus is the decision
paragraphs: Stumptown's current words are citrus, dark chocolate and raisin. They are roaster-attributed descriptors, not additives and not a score from Coffeedant. The combination separates Hair Bender from a purely smoky dark roast: the fruit could make a straight shot more interesting for one drinker and too sharp for another. Milk may shift attention toward the chocolate, but that is a reason to try your normal drink, not a guaranteed tasting outcome. [1]

Owner discussion illustrates that preference matters. In an r/espresso thread, some users reported enjoyable shots while another found the coffee too acidic for straight espresso. Those are individual bags, grinders and recipes, not representative product testing or a failure rate. Start with 12 oz rather than using a 5 lb order to settle a flavor question. [7]

sections.title: Keep two recipes for two brew methods
paragraphs: Stumptown's espresso guide uses Hair Bender at roughly 19.5 g in a portafilter and suggests a short 24–28 g beverage in about 23–28 seconds. That is a roaster starting recipe, not a target every basket or roast date must reach. The guide itself says dose, grind and extraction may need adjustment. If your basket is smaller, follow its safe dose range first. Record dose and beverage mass so changes have a meaning. [4]

For drip or pour-over, use the method-specific guide rather than taking the espresso grind into a filter. A dual-method household has a real workflow cost: a grinder may need a purge or repeatable return to the espresso setting. Hair Bender's versatility means the coffee can serve both methods; it does not make one grind setting serve both. Compare our grinder reviews before blaming the beans for a poor second brew. [1] [4] [8]

sections.title: The 12 oz bag is the useful first trial
paragraphs: Stumptown's freshness guidance emphasizes roast date, air exposure and whole-bean storage; its storage guidance cautions against repeatedly moving coffee between freezer and room temperature because of moisture. Keep the bag sealed in a cool, dry place and grind close to brewing. A grocery bag and a direct-order bag may have different shelf histories, so inspect the date and seal instead of treating the brand name as proof of freshness. [5] [6]

The 5 lb size is available, but a low cost per ounce is irrelevant if most of it loses the flavor you bought it for. At 18 g per espresso dose, 12 oz supplies roughly 18 doses before dialing waste; 5 lb supplies far more than most single drinkers can finish quickly. These are mass calculations, not shelf-life promises. Households with steady volume can reconsider bulk after testing the small bag.

sections.title: Compare the bag you will finish, not a discount banner
paragraphs: The direct product feed showed $19 for 12 oz and $105 for 5 lb on October 14, 2026. At the 12 oz price, beans cost about $0.056 per gram, or $1.00 for an illustrative 18 g dose before shipping, tax, milk and dialing waste. The 5 lb bag is cheaper per ounce, but requires enough consumption or careful portioning to justify it. The site also displays subscription promotions; those are not used as a permanent price. [1]

Hair Bender is more clearly documented as a multi-method coffee than many bags branded merely 'espresso.' That is a useful reason to pay attention to it if one household alternates methods. If your actual routine is only espresso with large milk drinks, compare a more explicitly milk-focused blend before assuming versatility is a benefit.

sections.title: Choose the next bag for the missing trait
paragraphs: Stumptown Holler Mountain is the same-roaster alternative when a medium, organic coffee with a citrus-caramel-berry brief sounds better. Counter Culture Hologram gives a medium fruit-and-milk-chocolate direction and a more explicit roast-date component selector. Onyx Monarch moves toward a darker chocolate and milk-drink role. These are source-led comparisons, not a Coffeedant blind tasting. [1] [9]

If citrus is the part you actively avoid, do not buy Hair Bender just because it is a famous café espresso. A smaller bag of a more roast-forward product is a cleaner test. If you mainly drink black filter coffee, compare the roaster's Holler Mountain or a current single origin and make the decision on your own brew.

faqs.answer: No. This is a research-led buying assessment; the flavor words belong to Stumptown and individual owners are attributed.

faqs.question: Is Hair Bender a dark roast?
faqs.answer: Stumptown's signature-blend collection calls it medium/dark. It is not the same purchase brief as a smoky French roast.

faqs.question: Can I use it for drip as well as espresso?
faqs.answer: Yes. Stumptown explicitly lists both uses. They require different grinds and recipes.

faqs.question: Are the origins fixed?
faqs.answer: No fixed component list is promised. The roaster describes a changing blend drawing on several regions.

faqs.question: Which size should I buy first?
faqs.answer: The 12 oz whole-bean bag is a sensible trial; buy 5 lb only if your consumption and storage plan justify it.

faqs.question: What is a starting espresso recipe?
faqs.answer: Stumptown demonstrates about 19.5 g in and 24–28 g out, then advises adjusting dose and grind to the actual equipment and coffee.

methodology: I compared the official Hair Bender product and Shopify variant feed, Stumptown's blend explanation, its method-specific brew advice, freshness guidance and a self-selected owner discussion. The owner accounts explain possible preferences; they do not establish a mean taste, defect rate or test score. Coffeedant has not bought, brewed, tasted or measured this coffee.

The product and price record was checked October 14, 2026 for the US direct market. Composition, roast date, shipping and discounts can change. This page attributes sensory language to the roaster and leaves unlisted farm, variety and current component percentages unknown.
finalTitle: Start with the 12 oz bag and two recipes
finalVerdict: Hair Bender is worth investigating when espresso and drip both matter and you want Stumptown's chocolate-plus-citrus direction. Begin with 12 oz, inspect the roast date and keep distinct espresso and filter settings. If your first bag is too bright or your household drinks only large lattes, choose a more focused alternative rather than assuming a different pack size will solve the mismatch.

title: Stumptown Holler Mountain review: an organic medium blend for espresso and drip
description: A research-led look at Stumptown Holler Mountain whole beans, attributed citrus-caramel-berry notes, medium roast, organic claim, dual-method fit, storage and US price.
imageAlt: Official Stumptown Holler Mountain whole-bean bag
imageCredit: Official Stumptown product photograph for identification; no Coffeedant tasting or photography.
verdict: Holler Mountain is a sensible one-bag option for a home that alternates drip and espresso and prefers a roaster-described medium roast to a darker café blend. Stumptown calls it organic and describes citrus, caramel and berry jam. Those are the roaster's notes, not flavors Coffeedant verified; the real test is a fresh small bag in both of your normal brewers.
bestFor: Households alternating drip coffee and espresso
A medium-roast, organic-labeled blend with a caramel and fruit direction
Buyers willing to inspect roast date before buying at retail
skipIf: You need a fixed single-origin farm or variety
You want a deliberately dark, smoky profile
You will not finish a 5 lb bag while it still suits your palate

sections.title: The repeatable name covers a changing blend
paragraphs: Stumptown describes Holler Mountain as an organic hometown blend and explicitly positions it for espresso and everyday drip. A blend name is an intended flavor target, not a lot number. Its blend explainer says year-round products are built from changing coffees selected for each component's role. Do not infer an unchanged farm, variety or processing method from the package name alone. [1] [2]

The roaster's whole-bean category calls Holler Mountain medium roast. That is more useful than a vague 'balanced' label when you compare it with French Roast or Hair Bender, but it is still a roaster classification rather than an instrument reading on the bag in your hand. Certification and medium roast also answer separate questions: organic sourcing is not a measured taste or freshness guarantee. [3]

sections.title: Caramel is a bridge between the citrus and berry words
paragraphs: Stumptown lists citrus, caramel and berry jam. They are the roaster's sensory brief. A medium blend with that brief could be interesting black and still bring sweetness to milk, but Coffeedant has not tasted this coffee and cannot promise which note your grinder, water or batch will emphasize. If you want nearly no fruit impression, the official descriptors are a reason to start elsewhere. [1]

An independent Holler Mountain reviewer reported results over a particular four-week brewing period. That gives a sample-based perspective, but cannot make every shipment taste the same. The useful buyer question is whether you prefer the Holler Mountain brief over Hair Bender's darker chocolate and raisin direction. Try equal-size fresh bags in your actual drink instead of treating either reviewer's preference as a ranking. [7]

sections.title: Versatility costs a second grinder setting
paragraphs: The roaster says Holler Mountain can pull espresso and serve as a daily drip coffee. That removes a product suitability doubt, but it does not mean one recipe transfers. Stumptown's method index separates espresso, automatic drip and manual filter because dose, grind and contact time differ. Use your basket's dose for espresso and a filter recipe for drip, recording results separately. [1] [4]

If the household alternates every morning, consider whether your grinder can return to the prior espresso setting without repeated waste. A hopper full of Holler Mountain will not fix a grinder that cannot make the needed adjustment. For milk drinks, dial the shot before judging how caramel or berry language reads in milk; a large latte can hide differences that show up clearly in black drip.

sections.title: Check the date on the channel you use
paragraphs: Stumptown sells direct and through retail partners. Those channels can have different time between roast and purchase. Inspect the bag's roast date and package condition rather than assuming a grocery bag and a direct shipment are equivalent. Stumptown's freshness and storage articles favor keeping whole beans protected from air and moisture and caution against repeatedly moving an opened bag in and out of the freezer. [5] [6]

At 12 oz, the bag offers roughly nineteen 18 g espresso doses before dialing waste. A 5 lb bag offers far more; the larger format makes sense only if your household consumes enough or has a portioning plan. There is no universal number of days this blend stays enjoyable in every kitchen, so use the first small bag to learn your own consumption and flavor curve.

sections.title: The direct price is a dated starting point
paragraphs: The official US feed showed $20 for 12 oz and $110 for 5 lb on October 14, 2026. At $20 for 12 oz, the illustrative bean cost is about $0.059 per gram or $1.06 for an 18 g espresso dose before shipping, tax, milk and grinder waste. A subscription promotion may lower checkout price, but it has separate terms; it is not the base comparison in this review. [1]

That figure is close to Hair Bender's direct 12 oz price at this check. The buying decision should turn on your preferred roast direction, use of organic certification and whether the roast date available to you is satisfactory. Paying for a huge bag you cannot finish is not a saving.

sections.title: Change the coffee only when you know why
paragraphs: Hair Bender is the same-roaster move toward a medium/dark café espresso recipe and dark-chocolate anchor. Counter Culture Hologram offers a medium fruit-and-milk-chocolate blend with a roast-date component selector. Apollo leans toward washed Ethiopian citrus and floral notes. The comparisons describe roaster briefs, not an in-house tasting order. [8] [9]

If you mostly drink filter coffee and need exact lot transparency, a current single origin may be more informative than any year-round blend. If you mostly make large milk drinks and want more roast presence, an espresso-focused darker blend may fit better. Holler Mountain's strength is the middle ground only when the middle ground is your actual routine.

finalTitle: Try the small bag in both brewers
finalVerdict: Holler Mountain is a credible dual-method candidate if a medium, organic blend and Stumptown's citrus-caramel-berry brief match your household. Keep two recipes and check the roast date. If one method dominates, a more focused coffee may be a better purchase than a larger bag of a compromise.
